§10.3.3 Values Are Verbatim

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-values-are-verbatim · forms fidelity

✅ Normative

Entered content MUST be transcribed exactly as it appears on the page. A value MUST NOT be rounded, reformatted, computed or summarised.

This is Cell Text Fidelity§9.6.3 applied to what someone wrote into a field.

Printed Output Not
29,513 29,513 29513, 29,513.00
590.50 590.50 590.5
1.0000000000 % 1.0000000000 % 1.0%, 1
-599,459 -599,459 (599,459)
(284,791) (284,791) -284,791

A negative amount MUST keep the form the page printed: a leading minus stays a minus, parentheses stay parentheses. Converting between them is a reformat, and a reformat is how a value stops matching the document it came from.

Identifiers are not normalised either

An entered SSN, TIN, policy number or account number MUST be transcribed exactly as printed. It MUST NOT be rewritten to a canonical mask such as XXX-XX-XXXX or re-grouped to a standard shape.

This holds however the form splits the digits. A social security number printed across three boxed groups is the printed digits, in the grouping the page uses:

- \[E\] **Partner's SSN or TIN**: 27-4162256

Normalising an identifier looks harmless because the canonical form is more readable. It is the same failure as rounding a number: the output stops matching the document, and a reader verifying a value against the page finds a string that is not on it. A consumer that needs a canonical form can derive one; it cannot recover the printed one.

Split dollar and cent columns

A form that prints dollars and cents in two ruled columns holds one value. It MUST be rendered as one value — 1,234.00 — and MUST NOT be split across two fields. The rule lines are typesetting, not structure.
